cards.f: Why does a warm-up reduce injury?
cards.b: Warmer muscles are more elastic, blood flow rises and joints are lubricated, so less chance of strains.
Return the body to rest, remove waste such as lactic acid, reduce soreness.
Damage to a ligament (bone to bone), e.g. twisted ankle.
Damage to a muscle or tendon, e.g. pulled hamstring.
A broken bone that breaks through the skin. Also called compound.
A bone forced out of its normal position in a joint.
Stop play at once, do not return the same day, seek medical help.
Build muscle and strength. Risks: liver damage, high blood pressure, aggression.
Slow heart rate, reduce tremor. Used in archery and shooting. Risk: low blood pressure.
Remove water to lose weight quickly or mask drugs. Risk: dehydration and cramps.
Increases red blood cells for endurance. Risk: blood clots, stroke, heart attack.
Re-infusing stored blood to raise red blood cell count. Banned. Risks: clots and infection.
World Anti-Doping Agency. Sets the banned list and organises testing.

short.q: Explain two ways a coach can reduce injury risk in a school football match.
short.model: Make sure players warm up and wear shin pads. Check the pitch for hazards and enforce the rules so dangerous tackles are stopped.

short.q: Describe how to treat a sprained ankle.
short.model: Use PRICE: rest and protect the ankle, apply wrapped ice, compress with a bandage and raise it above the heart. Seek medical help if severe.

short.q: Give one effect and one risk of stimulants.
short.model: They increase alertness and delay fatigue. Risks include addiction, raised blood pressure and heart problems.

short.q: Why are performance-enhancing drugs banned in sport?
short.model: They give an unfair advantage, so they are cheating. They also damage health and set a bad example for young people.

short.q: Explain why diuretics are misused in boxing.
short.model: Diuretics remove water, so a boxer can lose weight quickly to make a lower weight category. They can also mask other drugs.
